_meta.description: Pre-parsed ASIC conduct reference content, extracted once into structured form and ingested deterministically via transport:s3 + mode:map. Obligations are durable statutory/RG knowledge; precedents are landmark, publicly-documented conduct matters. No individual conduct assessments (run conclusions).

obligations.title: Provide financial services efficiently, honestly and fairly
obligations.description: An AFS licensee must do all things necessary to ensure the financial services covered by its licence are provided efficiently, honestly and fairly — an overarching conduct standard enforced by ASIC and the courts.

obligations.title: Internal dispute resolution (RG 271)
obligations.description: Financial firms must operate an internal dispute resolution (IDR) system meeting ASIC's enforceable standards, including a maximum 30-calendar-day response timeframe and prescribed IDR response content.

obligations.title: Design and distribution obligations (DDO, RG 274)
obligations.description: Issuers must make a target market determination (TMD) for financial products, distribute consistently with it, take reasonable distribution steps, monitor outcomes and review the TMD. Distributors must not distribute outside the target market.

obligations.title: Reportable situations / breach reporting (RG 78)
obligations.description: AFS and credit licensees must report 'reportable situations' (significant breaches and likely breaches) to ASIC, generally within 30 days of first knowing of, or being reckless as to, a reportable situation.

obligations.title: Best interests duty (personal advice)
obligations.description: A provider of personal financial advice to retail clients must act in the best interests of the client and prioritise the client's interests over its own where there is a conflict.

obligations.title: Anti-hawking prohibition
obligations.description: A person must not offer a financial product for issue or sale to a retail client in the course of, or because of, unsolicited contact.

obligations.title: Conflicted remuneration ban (RG 246)
obligations.description: Benefits that could reasonably influence financial product advice given to retail clients (conflicted remuneration) are generally prohibited under the FoFA reforms.

precedents.issue: Charging ongoing advice/service fees to customers where no service was provided ('fee for no service'), and inadequate records to demonstrate service delivery — a systemic issue surfaced by the Financial Services Royal Commission.
precedents.outcome: Sector-wide remediation exceeding AUD 4.7 billion to affected customers, multiple ASIC actions and civil penalties.
precedents.lesson: Charging for a service not rendered, with poor evidence of delivery, is a systemic conduct failure attracting large-scale remediation and penalties — controls must evidence that recurring fees map to services actually provided.

precedents.issue: Responsible-lending test case on whether declared living expenses (and the Household Expenditure Measure benchmark) must be verified line-by-line when assessing loan suitability (the 'wagyu and shiraz' case).
precedents.outcome: The Full Federal Court dismissed ASIC's appeal, finding the responsible-lending provisions did not mandate line-by-line expense verification.
precedents.lesson: Responsible-lending obligations are outcome-focused rather than prescriptive on expense verification — but firms still bear the onus of a reasonable suitability assessment; litigation clarified, not removed, the duty.

precedents.issue: Design-and-distribution failures — deficient or missing target market determinations, or distribution beyond the defined target market, for retail financial and credit products.
precedents.outcome: ASIC has issued numerous interim stop orders halting the offer/distribution of affected products until TMDs are remediated.
precedents.lesson: DDO non-compliance triggers rapid regulatory intervention (stop orders) that halts distribution — TMDs must be robust and distribution genuinely consistent with them.
